newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks lower, short lull foreseen.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks lower, short lull foreseen.

text.p: Croatian stocks were mostly lower in lacklustre trade on Wednesday and market participants foresaw a short lull, extending into the next week.
"These are only corrections of prices, not a downward trend," Igor Kos of Taurus brokerage told Reuters.
He expected prices to fluctuate slightly for some time amid investor reluctance to enter big transactions while awaiting results of local elections, due in April.
Nine of 13 active issues fell, three rose and one was unchanged. Turnover slid to 3.7 million kuna from 4.0 million, on a slightly higher volume of 10,360 shares.
Cable maker Elka stood out as the day's biggest gainer, rising five kuna to 180 on a high volume of 1,954. But traders said there was demand for some 3,000 shares, outstripping the current supply.
"If this keeps up, the price will move up," said Hrvoje Poljak, analyst at I.F.C. consultancy and brokerage.
Zagreb's Hotel Intercontinental led decliners, losing 70 kuna to 120, but sold only eight shares. It last traded in October 1996.
Four of five active seaside hoteliers were also on the losing side with a few hundred shares in each changing hands, save for Riviera from Porec that sold 1,608 ending at 183 kuna.
Only the Pula-based Arenaturist rose five kuna to 180 with 520 shares sold.
Most actively traded was food company Podravka, which closed 3.9 kuna lower at 314 on volume of 2,650 shares.
Chocolate maker Kras was flat at 520 kuna with 1,703 shares sold.
Fully-listed Pliva pharmaceutical stock edged down 10 kuna to 470 on volume of 628 shares.
Another blue chip, Zagrebacka Banka ordinary shares, closed one kuna lower at 1,829 kuna with 87 units sold.
